title: Relationships Start Off On The Right Track; But Shaw Festival's Spotlight On

display_heading.headline: Relationships Start Off On The Right Track

contact_edits.before: Back in Toronto, I recommend Fear of Flight, though more for its presentation than its substance. Originating (quite some time ago) with the Artistic Fraud company of Newfoundland, this depicts a storm-tossed cross-country plane trip, with vignettes of the passengers' past lives supplied by playwrights from all points along the flight path. Only one of these (written by Daniel MacIvor, performed by Mia Mansfield as an innocent lady travelling at the behest of Jesus, who in this incarnation sounds like a con man) is especially enlivening, but it's the group effort that counts. While hanging firmly on to their individual identities, the 14 actors combine brilliantly in a kind of acted ballet to which they also provide non-stop a cappella accompaniment. Jillian Keiley's production justifies the mountainous regard in which she's held across Canada. Actually, she'd already done that, for me, with her magnificent staging of Creon, the penultimate play in Ned Dickens's City of Wine cycle. The ultimate one, too--Seven, directed by Sarah Garton Stanley -- was a fine piece of vocal and visual orchestration, with the highest overall standard of acting (by mature York students) of the entire enterprise. Both plays brought the chorus to the forefront of the action: brilliantly so in Creon, which brought the Antigone story to new life, with too much repetition but to ultimately stirring effect in Seven. Collecting these last two episodes confirmed some of my earlier preconceptions, overturned others. Somebody remount the whole thing so I can write about it again. - Brief Encounters is in repertory through Oct. 24 at the Festival Theatre, Niagara-on-the-Lake. Call 1-800-511-SHAW for tickets. Fear of Flight runs through May 24 at the Factory Theatre. Call 416-504-9971 for details.
